title: I built this for traders who care about what happens after the signal fires.
author: Aryan_Das
selftext:
I'm building GM Markets, it's an infra which lets people outside the US buy fractional US stocks and commodities using stablecoins.

You deposit USDC or USDT from your wallet and buy what you want and hold it as a token backed 1:1 by real shares at a regulated US broker. Proof of reserves is on chain, the spreads 0.10 to 0.20 percent and gas handled by us plus we will also add card and apple pay soon enough for non crypto users.

Our first results are strong and we're looking for traders to give us a genuine feedback.

I'm looking for brutally honest feedback on this, something that will help us get ready for the big leagues.

Thanks in advance!

comments.author: AdditionalHold3296
comments.body: looks interesting, is there a live product or demo I can try?

replies.author: Aryan_Das
replies.body: Sure you can try it out here, it's in beta. You can search GM Markets.

replies.author: AdditionalHold3296
replies.body: The value proposition is interesting, but the landing page doesn't immediately explain why I'd use this over a traditional broker...can you explain

replies.author: Aryan_Das
replies.body: Fair point, the core difference is that we're optimizing for global users who already hold stablecoins and instead of wire transfers, FX, and banking friction, they can invest directly from USDC/USDT into tokenized US equities backed 1:1 by real shares and yes THANKS for pointing this out we definitely need to make that clearer above the fold.

replies.author: Adnanali-
replies.body: Interesting approach. i would like to point How do you handle things like stock splits, dividends, and voting rights for tokenized equities? That's something I'd definitely want to understand before using it.

comments.author: ConstantRock386
comments.body: The onboarding flow could do a better job explaining what happens after I deposit stablecoins.

replies.author: Aryan_Das
replies.body: Ah yes agreed, we've been focused on keeping onboarding simple but that shouldn't come at the cost of clarity. We'll add better explanations around deposit confirmations, settlement and what users should expect before they place their first trade.

comments.author: Vrad01
comments.body: The onboarding flow could do a better job explaining what happens after I deposit stablecoins.

comments.author: Vrad01
comments.body: The platform needs more social proof before I'd feel comfortable moving larger amounts.

replies.author: Aryan_Das
replies.body: We have a transparency section on our website. You can have a look at that for social proves.

comments.author: Legitimate-Film-4309
comments.body: Some screens prioritize aesthetics over information density, which may frustrate active traders.

replies.author: Aryan_Das
replies.body: we've optimized for simplicity first but yeah you're right active traders need more data at a glance. As we roll out advanced views, the goal is to keep the clean experience while giving power users the information they need.

comments.author: IndependentGuard4414
comments.body: There's a lot of emphasis on low fees but not enough on why I should trust the platform with my money.

comments.author: Adnanali-
comments.body: This looks interesting, especially for users outside the US. One thing I'd want to understand better is what happens if GM Markets shuts down or runs into financial issues. Since the stocks are tokenized, how are user assets protected and can users still redeem their holdings independently?

comments.author: True_Interaction_994
comments.body: Interesting idea. The biggest thing I’d want before using it is transparency around custody, regulation, and how redemptions actually work. The concept solves a real problem for non-US users, but trust and execution will matter more than features. Wishing you luck with the build.

replies.author: Aryan_Das
replies.body: Appreciate it, that's fair feedback and it's something we're actively improving and yeah I agree trust has to be earned, not assumed.

comments.author: therichprince
comments.body: I would not deposit or advise anyone to deposit funds into anything.

replies.body:
well I guess he is just asking for a feedback and for that you just need to sign up and as I can see you don't need to add funds to give a feedback???  
  
In fact I just signed up and gave them a feedback.....

replies.author: Aryan_Das
replies.body: I was trying to convey exactly this

comments.author: NoCartographer4725
comments.body: What’s the differnce between buying tokenized stocks from Jupiter or hyper liquid?

replies.author: Aryan_Das
replies.body:
good question, jupiter and hyperliquid give you perps, you're betting on price movement with funding rates and liquidation risk, you dont actually own the stock.

what we built is different, when you buy aapl on gm markets a real share gets held at a regulated us broker and you get a token backed 1:1 by it, no funding rates, no liquidation, it just sits in your wallet.

happy to answer anything else if youre curious.

comments.author: agonzamart
comments.body: This is a good project idea cool! 😎

replies.author: Aryan_Das
replies.body: Thanks for your compliment, would really love your valuable feedback on this.
